headline: High-risk filesystem and network interaction: OpenHands can write/browse/run code while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, creating default-path leakage and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read/write runtime files, run browsers, and use MCP, so it may ingest content from nuwa-skill if the pair shares files or an MCP bridge. nuwa-skill’s allowlisted egress can also carry attacker-controlled content into OpenHands workflows. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF the two agents share a mounted workspace or MCP server, then prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF OpenHands parses nuwa-skill output as instructions, then attacker-controlled content can steer actions.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP servers between the agents.
Separate their workspaces or mounted volumes.
Treat nuwa-skill outputs as untrusted text in OpenHands.
Add a manual review step before any tool-using action.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands explicitly touches files mounted into its runtime and handles model provider API keys, while nuwa-skill has network egress allowed by policy. If both see the same mounted files, sensitive file contents can flow from OpenHands into nuwa-skill’s outbound path. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF both agents are attached to the same mounted volume, then file contents can be exposed across the pair.
IF OpenHands processes secrets from mounted files, then those secrets may be forwarded through nuwa-skill egress.
mitigations: Use separate mounted volumes for each agent.
Remove secrets from any shared runtime files.
Restrict nuwa-skill egress to a narrower allowlist.
Rotate any API keys exposed in mounted files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses inside its runtime; nuwa-skill has network egress and is a scientific-research agent that may also act on files or outputs, but its write surfaces are not documented. Because the pair could contend over the same mounted volume or git state and uncertainty must escalate, the safest supported rating is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, then concurrent writes can corrupt state.
IF nuwa-skill writes through an undocumented surface, then conflicts with OpenHands become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate repositories or branches.
Serialize git writes with a lock file.
Avoid shared writable mounts.
Run one agent at a time for mutating tasks.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands is an action-taking coding agent with shell, browser, and editor loops, so if it consumes nuwa-skill output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into code or runtime actions. nuwa-skill’s documented egress suggests it can supply content, but there is no direct evidence of verification between them. This is a default-path risk only if outputs are chained without review.
conditions: IF OpenHands uses nuwa-skill output as a task spec without verification, then errors can propagate into actions.
IF nuwa-skill emits fabricated facts that OpenHands executes, then downstream mistakes can affect files or commands.
mitigations: Require human review before execution.
Add a verification step for all cross-agent outputs.
Limit OpenHands to read-only mode for the first pass.
Use structured schemas for handoff messages.
requires-engineering: implement citation checking before action execution.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenHands handles model provider API keys and runs in a Docker runtime by default, while nuwa-skill is only documented as a research agent with allowlisted egress. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a small compliance gap is plausible from secret handling and outbound traffic. The other agent is not cited for a specific compliance regime because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into OpenHands runtime files, then retention and logging controls must be checked.
IF nuwa-skill egress reaches a non-approved endpoint, then policy review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the runtime.
Review outbound allowlists.
Confirm retention settings for logs and artifacts.
Store secrets in a dedicated vault.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
